title: Home and community-based services policy and waivers
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
proposal: Show a fictional waiver-document request moving through submission, review and a request for more information; mark where the proposed extra document creates a repeat trip, then compare an alternative that addresses the same concern.
purpose: Make documentation and authorization burden visible before discussing an option.
learnerAction: Mark one unnecessary repeat step and write an alternative to discuss with the policy owner.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Sets policy for waiver and community-based services, including eligibility, service menus, rates, and provider standards. Existing entry points: Who gets which service mix and why; Burden of documentation and authorization steps; Language and format of notices; Provider capacity in different communities.
accessibleEquivalent: Equivalent ordered steps and a text comparison table; no information conveyed by color alone.

title: MnCHOICES assessment and access
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
media: Short Blender scene sequence with annotated service journey
proposal: Replay a first-contact conversation in which the worker checks communication preferences and offers a staffed way to complete assessment planning; pause before the next handoff.
purpose: Connect language, access and supported decision-making with the actual assessment route.
learnerAction: Write the first question to ask and identify who owns the next accessible contact.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Governs how people are assessed for and connected to long-term services and supports. Existing entry points: First contact in the person's language; Accessibility of the assessment process; Person-centered practice and supported decision-making; Wait times and follow-up by community.
accessibleEquivalent: Full dialogue, descriptions of actions and a keyboard-usable text journey beside captioned media.

title: Support planning and case management
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
proposal: Compare a plan organized around provider availability with one that first records the person's stated goal and the questions still to resolve; highlight the changed wording.
purpose: Show how a planning conversation affects what is written in the plan.
learnerAction: Rewrite one fictional goal in the person's own terms and name an unanswered question.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Standards and support for the people who plan services with individuals and families. Existing entry points: Plans that reflect the person's goals; Cultural and linguistic responsiveness of planning conversations; Caseload and time as equity issues.
accessibleEquivalent: Both plan excerpts as selectable text, with annotations in reading order.

title: Positive supports and person-centered practice
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
media: Three-panel illustration with a reflection card
proposal: Show an abstract shared-room situation, the environmental demand that is getting in the way, and a proposed support to discuss; keep the example about changing the setting rather than diagnosing a person.
purpose: Examine restriction-versus-support assumptions and whose needs the current setting serves.
learnerAction: Identify the unsupported interpretation and one support question to bring to the responsible practitioner.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Guidance and oversight for positive support strategies and person-centered planning. Existing entry points: Restriction versus support; Whose behavior is treated as a problem; Access to positive supports across communities.
accessibleEquivalent: Described panels and identical reflection prompts in text; no diagnostic or treatment instructions.

title: Olmstead and community integration
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
proposal: Follow a fictional person's preferred community activity through transport, available support and a setting default; show where a choice is narrowed by the process.
purpose: Connect community integration with practical options and barriers rather than a generic inclusion image.
learnerAction: List the person's stated preference, one system barrier and a question for the responsible service partner.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Work toward services in the most integrated setting appropriate to the person. Existing entry points: Defaults that steer people to segregated settings; Community capacity by place; Data on who moves and who does not.
accessibleEquivalent: Labeled text nodes with a linear list of relationships and questions.

title: Employment and day services
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
proposal: Use a fictional employment goal to compare exploration, development and ongoing support questions, linking the existing Employment First and E1MN reference.
purpose: Make employment-first policy relevant to an individual's goal without predicting ability from identity or disability.
learnerAction: Choose which question needs answering before an employment option can be discussed.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Employment-first practice and day service policy. Existing entry points: Competitive integrated employment as the first option; Provider practice with different communities; Outcomes by disability, race, language, and place.
accessibleEquivalent: Accessible HTML comparison and original source links; visual is optional.

title: Early Intensive Developmental and Behavioral Intervention and children's services
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
proposal: Map a fictional family moving from an initial question to a service-planning conversation, with a language preference check and a clearly owned provider-availability follow-up.
purpose: Expose first-contact and provider-access questions without depicting a diagnostic process.
learnerAction: Identify a point where the family must repeat information and propose a more usable handoff question.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Services for children with autism and related conditions and their families. Existing entry points: Family language and cultural context in diagnosis and planning; Provider availability by community; Trust with families who have experienced the system badly.
accessibleEquivalent: Numbered text journey and dialogue transcript; no images presented as clinical guidance.

title: Brain injury, guardianship, and related programs
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
proposal: Present a fictional choice in plain language with time to ask questions and a chosen supporter; compare 'we will decide for you' wording with a question about what help the person wants.
purpose: Keep the person's role visible when discussing support, communication and presumed capability.
learnerAction: Rewrite one paternalistic question and identify the professional guidance needed for a rights decision.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Programs for people with brain injury and work related to guardianship and supported decision-making. Existing entry points: Supported decision-making before guardianship; Accessible communication about rights; Who is presumed capable.
accessibleEquivalent: All choices and sample wording available as plain text; no legal eligibility or capacity determination.

title: Contracts, grants, fiscal, and capacity work
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
media: Annotated fictional solicitation and application flow
proposal: Mark a hypothetical grant requirement, the effort needed to respond and an alternative way to demonstrate the relevant capability; keep dates and amounts as labeled placeholders.
purpose: Show how application requirements shape who can enter a funding process.
learnerAction: Write one question about the necessity of a requirement and who should review it.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Contracting, grants, rates, and capacity building for the division's providers and partners. Existing entry points: Who wins awards and who never applies; Requirements in solicitations; Reporting that shows who is served.
accessibleEquivalent: Selectable sample text with comments and a linear flow description.

title: Data, quality, and evaluation
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
proposal: Use invented counts to compare an overall result with grouped views and a suppressed view; show that more detail can reduce privacy and still fail to explain experience.
purpose: Make the limits of disaggregation and the contribution of qualitative evidence visible.
learnerAction: Explain which question a chart can answer, what it cannot show and what the data owner must decide.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Division data, quality assurance, and evaluation of services and outcomes. Existing entry points: Disaggregation with small-group protection; Systems built for billing rather than equity analysis; Qualitative evidence alongside numbers.
accessibleEquivalent: Equivalent data table and written conclusions; keyboard controls and no invented operational suppression threshold.

title: Training, communication, and strategic communications
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
proposal: Show a fictional scanned notice beside a structured, plainly written version with headings, next action and help route; demonstrate reading order in the example.
purpose: Connect plain language, accessible format and usable action in one communication.
learnerAction: Identify the missing next action and revise a heading and instruction.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Division learning, internal and external communication, and plain-language practice. Existing entry points: Plain language and accessible documents by default; Language access in every channel; Learning that is voluntary and private.
accessibleEquivalent: The complete structured notice and an ordered description of the walkthrough.

title: Division leadership, legislative work, and strategy
placement: Immediately after “Equity entry points”, before “Connected areas of work”.
proposal: Trace a fictional team improvement from recommendation to the role with decision authority, resource choice and report-back; show an unresolved approval step explicitly.
purpose: Connect decision rights, resourcing and communication with whether practical improvements happen.
learnerAction: Name the decision needed, the responsible role and what colleagues need to hear back.
readiness: Current source provides the entry points; proposed example is not authored. Link and publication availability must follow the existing program surface.
basis: Division direction, legislative coordination, and the DSD equity implementation plan. Existing entry points: Decision rights and bottlenecks; Funded and staffed equity commitments; Reporting back to staff on what changed.
accessibleEquivalent: Accessible relationship table and a short editable decision note.

title: A hiring panel keeps choosing the same kind of candidate
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
proposal: Pause as a panel rewards a confident delivery and familiar degree; show the same answer assessed against a stated duty and written rubric.
purpose: Separate observed evidence from impressions of fluency or familiarity.
learnerAction: Underline the evidence for a criterion, remove an unsupported rating rationale and open the job-relatedness check.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: A DSD unit has filled three positions in a year. Each time, the panel chose the candidate who interviewed most fluently and had a graduate degree. Two strong internal candidates with years of direct-support and community experience did not advance past screening. First existing question: What does each requirement predict about the work?
accessibleEquivalent: Full dialogue, visual-action descriptions and the same fictional rubric as accessible text.

title: A team member says they do not know what it takes to advance
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
proposal: Compare a vague 'keep doing good work' response with a conversation that identifies the actual role requirement, an available stretch assignment and the question reserved for HR.
purpose: Make the difference between encouragement, opportunity and classification authority concrete.
learnerAction: Draft one transparent development opportunity and one question for the appropriate HR partner.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: In a stay conversation, a team member says they have never been told what the next classification requires, that visible projects go to the same two people, and that they are considering leaving. First existing question: What does the next step actually require, and is it written anywhere?
accessibleEquivalent: Side-by-side text dialogue and a written opportunity outline.

title: An accommodation disappears during a leadership rotation
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
media: Transition handoff diagram with a short scene
proposal: Follow an acting-lead rotation through an invitation, access planning and cohort kickoff; pause where ownership is missing and show an accessible alternative to the timed activity.
purpose: Show how a transition can lose access even when an accommodation already exists.
learnerAction: Name the responsible roles and rewrite the invitation's access information using a fictional example.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: A DSD staff member with an established accommodation is selected for an acting lead assignment in another unit. The new unit does not know about the arrangement, the cohort kickoff uses timed small-group activities with no captions, and the person quietly withdraws from the rotation. First existing question: Who owns accommodations across each transition in this pathway, by name?
accessibleEquivalent: Numbered handoff description and accessible invitation text; no employee identity or accommodation record.

title: A waiver policy change is going to leadership next month
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
media: Before/after burden map with an options table
proposal: Draw the proposed extra waiver document into a fictional family journey and compare two ways to address the stated fraud concern without assuming the analysis result.
purpose: Make a still-changeable policy decision and its distributed burden easier to examine.
learnerAction: Record who may carry each step and draft a question about an alternative for the policy owner.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: A change to documentation requirements for a waiver service is scheduled for leadership approval in four weeks. The change was designed to reduce fraud risk. No one has yet asked which families will find the new requirement hardest to meet. First existing question: Does the equity policy require a scan or a full analysis here, and who confirms that?
accessibleEquivalent: Ordered journey steps and an accessible options table; retain the text questions and professional handoff.

title: Redesigning an assessment process without adding steps
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
proposal: Let the learner follow an online self-service route and a staffed alternative, including language support and supported decision-making; expose the point at which the draft assumes internet access.
purpose: Test the difference between staff efficiency and a usable service route.
learnerAction: Choose a route for a stated access need and identify a step that still needs an accountable owner.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: A DSD team is redesigning how people are assessed for services. Early drafts add a self-service online step that would save staff time. Some of the people assessed do not use English, do not have reliable internet, or need supported decision-making. First existing question: How does someone who does not use English or the internet complete this on the first try?
accessibleEquivalent: Keyboard-readable branching text with all routes available in a linear outline.

title: Community input requested after the decision is effectively final
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
proposal: Place the already-approved decision before the proposed listening session; distinguish what can still change and add the missing return to the previous year's input.
purpose: Help staff describe remaining influence honestly and avoid repeating extractive requests.
learnerAction: Rewrite the invitation to state what remains open, then name an existing relationship to consult.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: A program change has been approved and funded. A manager asks for listening sessions with affected communities before rollout. Two of those communities were asked similar questions last year by another DHS unit and never heard what happened. First existing question: What can this engagement still change? If nothing, how will you say so honestly?
accessibleEquivalent: Text timeline and editable invitation example; no simulated community endorsement.

title: Listening sessions are done. Now what?
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
proposal: Show a fictional response with four visible parts: what was heard, what changed, what could not change and why, and the next contact or chance to influence.
purpose: Turn rich listening notes into a specific, honest response without overpromising.
learnerAction: Draft a short report-back using the existing questions and select the formats needed by the participants.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: A DSD team completed listening sessions with families and providers. The notes are rich. The team is unsure what to send back and worries about promising things it cannot deliver. First existing question: What changed because of the sessions, specifically?
accessibleEquivalent: Complete report-back text and annotation list; any audio version has a matching transcript.

title: A required form cannot be completed with a screen reader
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
media: Captioned demonstration of an inaccessible and corrected fictional form
proposal: Show why a scanned image has no usable fields, then demonstrate the structured alternative and a clear temporary access route while the source is repaired.
purpose: Make the barrier and the need for source ownership tangible.
learnerAction: Identify the barrier, select the accessible alternative and name the form owner/accessibility handoff.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: A provider reports that a DSD form required for authorization cannot be completed with a screen reader and is only available as a scanned image. No one on the team knows who owns the form. First existing question: Who owns this form, and do they know?
accessibleEquivalent: Accessible HTML form example, labeled controls and written demonstration; never require use of the inaccessible sample.

title: First contact happens in English only
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
proposal: Contrast an English-only voicemail dead end with a fictional intake opening that offers a usable way to reach language support; show the follow-up owner rather than ending at 'translation available'.
purpose: Place language access at first contact rather than after a delayed callback.
learnerAction: Mark the failed step and write the question the line owner must resolve.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: Families calling a DSD intake line reach an English-only greeting and a voicemail. Interpretation is available once a staff member calls back, often days later. First existing question: How does a person who does not use English reach a human in their language on the first try?
accessibleEquivalent: Both call paths as text with audio descriptions; all necessary information visible without listening.

title: The same three people speak in every team meeting
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
proposal: Show the same agenda with rapid open discussion, then with advance questions, a quiet writing interval and a facilitator explaining how input affected a decision.
purpose: Make participation conditions observable without assigning a cultural explanation to quietness.
learnerAction: Separate observation from interpretation and revise one meeting practice plus the report-back.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: A DSD supervisor notices that the same three people speak in meetings while newer staff and staff from other backgrounds stay quiet. One person told the supervisor privately that speaking up once got them nowhere. First existing question: What changed in the last quarter because someone spoke up, and did the team hear about it?
accessibleEquivalent: Full scene script, descriptions of facilitation actions and an editable agenda.

title: A comment in a meeting landed badly and nobody addressed it
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
proposal: Use a generic unsupported group generalization without repeating a slur; pause, name the specific assumption, invite clarification and model a leader's next repair step.
purpose: Practice a leader response that examines the statement without asking harmed colleagues to do the teaching.
learnerAction: Write the first repair sentence and identify when the established confidential route is needed.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: During a planning meeting, a comment about a community's habits went unchallenged. Afterward, two staff members said they felt the room had endorsed it. The person who made the comment did not realize it caused harm. First existing question: Who will name what happened and take responsibility for repair?
accessibleEquivalent: Full dialogue and action description with text-only reflection choices.

title: Every equity change waits for one approval that never comes
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
proposal: Draw three fictional improvements waiting on the same unexplained step; replace the opaque box with the decision, responsible role and information needed, while leaving actual authority intact.
purpose: Make a process bottleneck and the cost of waiting specific enough to discuss.
learnerAction: Draft a decision record with the proposed change, rationale and person or role who can decide.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: Several DSD teams have equity improvements ready, each waiting on the same approval step. The step exists because of a past problem no one can describe. Staff have begun to treat the process as immovable. First existing question: Who actually holds the decision right for this step, and what would they need to decide?
accessibleEquivalent: Ordered step list and editable decision record; no animated organization hierarchy.

title: Service data by race would identify a handful of people
placement: After “The situation” and before “What to notice first”; end at “Questions to ask before acting” and retain “Who to involve”.
proposal: Show how two innocent-looking grouped tables can reveal a tiny subgroup; compare a coarser view, suppressed view and a clearly labeled qualitative summary.
purpose: Explain why more granular reporting can create disclosure risk without answering the work question.
learnerAction: Write a limitation statement and ask the data owner which disclosure controls apply.
readiness: Complete source situation, notice points, questions and handoff exist; proposed media is not authored.
basis: A DSD analyst is asked to report service outcomes by race and language for a rural county. In several groups the count is below ten. Leadership wants the numbers next week. First existing question: What is the smallest group you will report, and who set that rule?
accessibleEquivalent: Equivalent accessible tables and written deduction steps; use only invented data and no universal threshold.

title: Design the role and posting
placement: Within the selected stage, after “A DSD practice situation” and before “Try it in practice”; use the existing “Create my reflection” action.
proposal: Contrast an inherited degree line with a duty-linked requirement and two credible forms of evidence.
purpose: Connect a qualification with an essential duty before accepting a familiar requirement.
learnerAction: A revised requirement with a clear explanation of its connection to the work. Use “A practice I would like to try” and “How will I learn from what happens?” to prepare the next step.
readiness: Existing text/tool destination is available in source; proposed shared asset is not yet authored.
basis: What does the work actually require? Examine the difference between a necessary qualification and a familiar picture of who usually does the work. Existing situation: A DSD posting repeats a degree requirement from an earlier version. The team has not checked which duties require it or what other experience could demonstrate the capability.
accessibleEquivalent: Use the existing job-relatedness resource with a text annotation; create a separate visual only if the shared excerpt is insufficient.

title: Reach and welcome applicants
placement: Within the selected stage, after “A DSD practice situation” and before “Try it in practice”; use the existing “Create my reflection” action.
proposal: Follow one fictional vacancy announcement through familiar networks, a clearer description and an additional appropriate channel, marking where an applicant could get stuck.
purpose: Examine discoverability and application access before inferring a lack of interest.
learnerAction: An outreach and accessibility plan, with a question to check after recruitment. Use “A practice I would like to try” and “How will I learn from what happens?” to prepare the next step.
readiness: Source already supplies a situation, practice moves, reflection and work product; media remains proposed.
basis: Who can discover and navigate this opportunity? Inclusive recruitment concerns access to information, application processes, and networks as well as the reach of an announcement. Existing situation: A position reaches the same professional circles each time. Strong potential applicants may never see it or understand how their experience connects.
accessibleEquivalent: Accessible channel table and ordered applicant journey.

title: Interview and assess fairly
placement: Within the selected stage, after “A DSD practice situation” and before “Try it in practice”; use the existing “Create my reflection” action.
proposal: Pause on the applicant looking down, then compare the unsupported 'lacks confidence' impression with evidence in the answer for the agreed competency.
purpose: Practice an evidence-based rating without interpreting identity, eye contact or cultural traits.
learnerAction: A practice rating explained through the answer and the job criterion, rather than eye contact or assumed cultural traits. Use “A practice I would like to try” and “How will I learn from what happens?” to prepare the next step.
readiness: Source already supplies a situation, practice moves, reflection and work product; media remains proposed.
basis: What is evidence, and what am I interpreting? A diverse panel still needs shared, job-related criteria. Cultural knowledge invites curiosity; it does not tell us why an individual behaves a particular way. Existing situation: An applicant gives a relevant example while looking down. A panel member describes the applicant as lacking confidence. The group has not connected that impression to the competency being assessed.
accessibleEquivalent: Full transcript, fictional answer and rubric in accessible text.

title: Welcome and orient
placement: Within the selected stage, after “A DSD practice situation” and before “Try it in practice”; use the existing “Create my reflection” action.
proposal: Follow a fictional new colleague who completed required training but needs a cross-team contact; connect their question to orientation and a willing point of help.
purpose: Make relationships and informal process knowledge visible during welcoming.
learnerAction: A welcome map and a follow-up conversation about what helped or remains missing. Use “A practice I would like to try” and “How will I learn from what happens?” to prepare the next step.
readiness: Existing text/tool destination is available in source; proposed shared asset is not yet authored.
basis: What does someone need to belong and contribute? Orientation includes relationships, access, expectations, and the informal knowledge established colleagues can take for granted. Existing situation: A new DSD colleague completes required training but still does not know who can explain a cross-team process or where to ask an everyday question.
accessibleEquivalent: Use the existing orientation directory with an editable text welcome map.

title: Support everyday contribution
placement: Within the selected stage, after “A DSD practice situation” and before “Try it in practice”; use the existing “Create my reflection” action.
proposal: Show a written recommendation overlooked in a fast meeting, then show advance input and a facilitator explaining how the recommendation informs the work.
purpose: Distinguish useful contribution from visibility or a preferred speaking style.
learnerAction: A change to a meeting, feedback conversation, or assignment process and what participants found useful. Use “A practice I would like to try” and “How will I learn from what happens?” to prepare the next step.
readiness: Source already supplies a situation, practice moves, reflection and work product; media remains proposed.
basis: Whose work is heard, supported, and recognized? Feedback, workload, access, and recognition are repeated leadership decisions. Look at specific work and conditions rather than using a preferred communication style as the standard. Existing situation: A colleague contributes carefully considered written recommendations but speaks less in meetings. Their contribution is less visible when development opportunities are discussed.
accessibleEquivalent: Dialogue, described meeting actions and a written-feedback example.

title: Mentor, sponsor, and develop
placement: Within the selected stage, after “A DSD practice situation” and before “Try it in practice”; use the existing “Create my reflection” action.
proposal: Show an interested employee asking for a capability to practice, then distinguish useful advice from a concrete supported co-leading opportunity.
purpose: Make development possible through supported practice while keeping formal program eligibility separate.
learnerAction: A development plan linking a capability, supported practice, feedback, and a next conversation. Use “A practice I would like to try” and “How will I learn from what happens?” to prepare the next step.
readiness: Source already supplies a situation, practice moves, reflection and work product; media remains proposed.
basis: Can people begin growing before someone selects them? Mentoring offers perspective; sponsorship helps people access opportunities. Development should make room for self-expressed interest and different career aspirations. Existing situation: An interested employee is new to state service and cannot yet meet a formal institute's eligibility requirement. They can still develop through a supported practice opportunity.
accessibleEquivalent: Two complete dialogue transcripts and a text development outline.

title: Make advancement understandable
placement: Within the selected stage, after “A DSD practice situation” and before “Try it in practice”; use the existing “Create my reflection” action.
proposal: Use the supervisor-to-director example to link cross-team strategy, resource tradeoffs and division decisions with existing evidence and a supported practice gap.
purpose: Clarify readiness without promising selection or confusing opportunity with potential.
learnerAction: A role-to-skill map with evidence, a learning opportunity, and feedback from someone familiar with the work. Use “A practice I would like to try” and “How will I learn from what happens?” to prepare the next step.
readiness: Source already supplies a situation, practice moves, reflection and work product; media remains proposed.
basis: What would demonstrate readiness for different responsibilities? Clear pathways connect real role requirements with opportunities to develop and demonstrate capability. A learning portfolio supports a conversation; it does not guarantee selection. Existing situation: A supervisor is interested in a director role but has had little opportunity to work on cross-team strategy, resource tradeoffs, or a division-wide decision.
accessibleEquivalent: Accessible matrix and complete worked text example.

title: Listen, respond, and sustain
placement: Within the selected stage, after “A DSD practice situation” and before “Try it in practice”; use the existing “Create my reflection” action.
proposal: Replay a response to repeatedly cancelled learning time; compare offering another course with renegotiating time, priorities and an agreed return to the concern.
purpose: Show how a stay conversation can lead to a response to working conditions.
learnerAction: An agreed action, a responsible role, and a follow-up that checks the employee's experience. Use “A practice I would like to try” and “How will I learn from what happens?” to prepare the next step.
readiness: Source already supplies a situation, practice moves, reflection and work product; media remains proposed.
basis: What would make it easier to stay and thrive? A stay conversation is useful when it leads to a response. Career growth sits alongside workload, support, relationships, recognition, and the conditions of the work. Existing situation: A capable colleague wants to develop but repeatedly loses agreed learning time to urgent tasks. Another course invitation does not address the problem.
accessibleEquivalent: Complete dialogue and written action/responsible-role/follow-up card.

title: Build continuity and future leadership
placement: Within the selected stage, after “A DSD practice situation” and before “Try it in practice”; use the existing “Create my reflection” action.
media: Captioned handover walkthrough and continuity map
proposal: Show a fictional recurring process performed by a second colleague using the handover, stopping where the decision context is missing; connect that gap to an open development opportunity.
purpose: Test usable knowledge transfer while broadening access to practice.
learnerAction: A continuity plan with a development opportunity, knowledge-transfer product, and practical readiness check. Use “A practice I would like to try” and “How will I learn from what happens?” to prepare the next step.
readiness: Source already supplies a situation, practice moves, reflection and work product; media remains proposed.
basis: What capability must continue, and who can access the chance to develop it? Succession planning connects critical work, future capabilities, open development opportunities, and knowledge transfer. It should broaden readiness rather than quietly designate an heir. Existing situation: One person holds most of the knowledge for an important DSD process. The division needs continuity and more colleagues need a fair chance to learn that work.
accessibleEquivalent: Written walkthrough, accessible process outline and the existing continuity planner.

title: Learn from transitions and departures
placement: Within the selected stage, after “A DSD practice situation” and before “Try it in practice”; use the existing “Create my reflection” action.
media: Existing succession text and continuity planner
proposal: Use the existing succession explanation and continuity planner to compare a list of files with a usable handover. If the shared walkthrough is later authored, link it here rather than commissioning a second video.
purpose: Use transitions to improve the process without guessing why someone left.
